_about: SERIES SHELF of one-off translators: the Wisdom of the East series (Orient Press 1904, then John Murray, ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), the Edwardian pocket library of Asian texts in English. Round 60 holds the Chinese, Japanese and Tibetan volumes plus Claud Field's Alchemy of Happiness: Lionel Giles's Lieh Tzu (1912) and Lao Tzu (1904), Anton Forke's Yang Chu (1912), Cranmer-Byng's Lute of Jade (1909), Feast of Lanterns (1916) and Odes of Confucius (1905), Clara Walsh's Master-Singers of Japan (1910), Ken Hoshino's Way of Contentment (Kaibara Ekiken, 1913) and Millicent Morrison's Ti-Me-Kun-Dan (1925). Round 61 adds the Indian, Persian, Arabic, Hebrew and Egyptian volumes and two more Chinese classics: E. J. Thomas's Buddhist Scriptures (1913) and Vedic Hymns (1923), Barnett's Path of Light (Santideva, 1909), Wagiswara and Saunders's Dhammapada (1912), Majid and Cranmer-Byng's Ruba'iyat of Hafiz (1910), Lederer's Secret Rose Garden (Shabistari, 1920), Cranmer-Byng's Rose-Garden of Sa'di (1910), Wollaston's Scroll of Wisdom (1906), Magan Lal and Westbrook's Zeb-un-Nissa (1913), Baerlein's Abu'l-Ala (1909), Wortabet's Arabian Wisdom, Collins's Duties of the Heart (Bahya, 1904), Cohen's Ancient Jewish Proverbs (1911), Dennis's Burden of Isis (1910), Gorn Old's Book of History (1906) and Ku Hung-Ming's Conduct of Life (Zhongyong, 1906). Each title gates on its own translator. Printings before 1931 only. US public domain. Added 2026-10-17 by lane C (rounds 60-61); Adam may veto. No uids minted.

wisdom-of-the-east-lieh-tzu.work: Taoist Teachings from the Book of Lieh Tzu
wisdom-of-the-east-lieh-tzu.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1912

wisdom-of-the-east-lao-tzu.scan_edition: The Orient Press, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1904 (the first edition; the series moved to John Murray in 1905); Google scan of a Harvard copy

wisdom-of-the-east-yang-chu.of: Yang Zhu (Yang Chu), from the Liezi
wisdom-of-the-east-yang-chu.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1912; introduction by Hugh Cranmer-Byng
wisdom-of-the-east-yang-chu.note: Forke's German-trained translation from the Chinese, made for this series.

wisdom-of-the-east-lute-of-jade.of: Classical Chinese poets (Li Po, Tu Fu and others)
wisdom-of-the-east-lute-of-jade.scan_edition: Project Gutenberg #390, transcribed (its note says) from a New York edition of 1909 of the Wisdom of the East volume
wisdom-of-the-east-lute-of-jade.note: Verse renderings, freer than a literal translation.

wisdom-of-the-east-feast-of-lanterns.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1916; Princeton Theological Seminary copy. The title page says 'rendered with an introduction by L. Cranmer-Byng'
wisdom-of-the-east-feast-of-lanterns.note: Verse renderings, like A Lute of Jade.

wisdom-of-the-east-odes.scan_edition: E. P. Dutton, New York, Wisdom of the East series, second edition, 1908 (first edition February 1905)
wisdom-of-the-east-odes.note: Verse renderings of selected odes, not a complete or literal Shijing.

wisdom-of-the-east-master-singers.of: Japanese poets from the Manyoshu onward
wisdom-of-the-east-master-singers.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1910; Royal Asiatic Society Bombay copy

wisdom-of-the-east-way-of-contentment.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1913

wisdom-of-the-east-ti-me-kun-dan.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1925; Digital Library of India scan
wisdom-of-the-east-ti-me-kun-dan.note: Morrison's introduction says she made her version word by word from the Tibetan text and that it varies much from Jacques Bacot's French translation.

wisdom-of-the-east-alchemy-of-happiness.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series (ed. L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia), 1910; Digital Library of India scan
wisdom-of-the-east-alchemy-of-happiness.note: Translated from the Hindustani, not the Persian, as the title page says. Field's Confessions of Al Ghazzali (same series) is on the claud-field shelf.

wisdom-of-the-east-buddhist-scriptures.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1913

wisdom-of-the-east-vedic-hymns.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1923

wisdom-of-the-east-path-of-light.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1909; Princeton Theological Seminary copy. The title page says 'rendered for the first time'

wisdom-of-the-east-way-of-virtue.translator: W. D. C. Wagiswara and K. J. Saunders
wisdom-of-the-east-way-of-virtue.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1912; Trinity College Toronto copy
wisdom-of-the-east-way-of-virtue.note: Max Müller's and F. L. Woodward's Dhammapadas are on the muller and singles-arts-miscellany shelves: different translations.

wisdom-of-the-east-rubaiyat-of-hafiz.translator: Syed Abdul Majid and L. Cranmer-Byng
wisdom-of-the-east-rubaiyat-of-hafiz.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series; first edition October 1910, this the March 1919 reprint. Translated with introduction by Syed Abdul Majid, rendered into English verse by L. Cranmer-Byng

wisdom-of-the-east-secret-rose-garden.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1920. The title page says 'rendered from the Persian'

wisdom-of-the-east-rose-garden-of-sadi.work: The Rose-Garden of Sa'di (from the Gulistan)
wisdom-of-the-east-rose-garden-of-sadi.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, third impression, 1910; Digital Library of India scan
wisdom-of-the-east-rose-garden-of-sadi.note: Selections, 'selected and rendered' by Cranmer-Byng; his note says the translation was prepared with the help of S. A. Kapadia.

wisdom-of-the-east-scroll-of-wisdom.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1906; University of Toronto copy
wisdom-of-the-east-scroll-of-wisdom.note: The title page names Wollaston only for the introduction, but his signed introduction (May 1906) presents the book as a new translation: no other English version is in print, 'therefore, no apology is needed for the present work'.

wisdom-of-the-east-diwan-of-zeb-un-nissa.translator: Magan Lal and Jessie Duncan Westbrook
wisdom-of-the-east-diwan-of-zeb-un-nissa.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1913; University of Toronto copy

wisdom-of-the-east-diwan-of-abul-ala.scan_edition: Project Gutenberg #13086, from the Wisdom of the East volume, second edition (Murray, 1909)
wisdom-of-the-east-diwan-of-abul-ala.note: English verse. Baerlein's dedication says E. J. Dillon had been putting the poet into English prose and that this book puts him into English verse. Not the same book as Ameen Rihani's Luzumiyat on singles-plays-poetry-2.

wisdom-of-the-east-arabian-wisdom.scan_edition: Project Gutenberg #33109, from the Wisdom of the East volume, third impression (Murray, 1916)

wisdom-of-the-east-duties-of-the-heart.scan_edition: The Orient Press, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1904
wisdom-of-the-east-duties-of-the-heart.note: Collins calls his version 'sometimes literal, now and again a summarised paraphrase'.

wisdom-of-the-east-jewish-proverbs.scan_edition: E. P. Dutton, New York, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1911
wisdom-of-the-east-jewish-proverbs.note: 'Compiled and classified' by Cohen, whose preface says he differs from Dukes's German collection 'in translation and interpretation'.

wisdom-of-the-east-burden-of-isis.of: Ancient Egyptian (the Lamentations of Isis and Nephthys)
wisdom-of-the-east-burden-of-isis.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1910

wisdom-of-the-east-book-of-history.work: The Classics of Confucius: Book of History
wisdom-of-the-east-book-of-history.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series, 1906; Google scan
wisdom-of-the-east-book-of-history.note: 'Rendered and compiled' by Gorn Old: an abridgement, not a complete Shujing. James Legge's complete version is on the legge shelf.

wisdom-of-the-east-conduct-of-life.work: The Conduct of Life, or the Universal Order of Confucius
wisdom-of-the-east-conduct-of-life.scan_edition: John Murray, London, in the Wisdom of the East series; first edition February 1906, this the October 1928 reprint

_pending.women-and-wisdom-of-japan: Women and Wisdom of Japan (Murray, 1905; india.history.resource.91283): the Onna Daigaku and its sequel in English, but the title page names only Shingoro Takaishi as writer of the introduction, and the text read so far never says who translated. Held back until the translator is established.
_pending.legends-of-indian-buddhism: Legends of Indian Buddhism (Murray, 1911; india.history.resource.112118): six legends translated from Burnouf's French, but the title page names Winifred Stephens only for the introduction and the text read never says who translated. Held back with Women and Wisdom of Japan until the translator is established.

_excluded.musings-of-a-chinese-mystic: Musings of a Chinese Mystic (Lionel Giles, 1906; musingschinesem00zhua): selections from H. A. Giles's 1889 Chuang Tzu translation, which its own note credits and which the giles shelf already holds whole.
_excluded.sayings-of-confucius: Lionel Giles's Sayings of Confucius (1907) is already on the giles shelf (PG 46389).
_excluded.held-in-singles: Already held on lane C's singles shelves: Gunn's Instruction of Ptah-hotep (PG 30508, singles-ideas), Bronnle's Awakening of the Soul (PG 34572, singles-ideas) and Ivan Chen's Book of Filial Duty (PG 75878, singles-ideas-3), and A. Hart Edwards's Bustan of Sadi (1911; PG 60471, singles-plays-poetry-2).
_excluded.confessions-of-al-ghazzali: Claud Field's Confessions of Al Ghazzali (1909) is already on the claud-field shelf.
_excluded.not-translations: Studies rather than translations, so off a translators' shelf: Yone Noguchi's Spirit of Japanese Poetry (1914, his lectures), E. V. Gatenby's Cloud-Men of Yamato (1929, 'an outline of mysticism in Japanese literature'), and M. A. Murray's Ancient Egyptian Legends (1913), which she says she 'retold ... in my own way'.
_excluded.wisdom-of-the-apocrypha: The Wisdom of the Apocrypha (1910) uses the Revised Version text (its prefatory note says so), so it is not a new translation.
_excluded.religion-of-the-koran: Wollaston's Religion of the Koran (1904): its Koran passages are 'taken from the Translation by the late Professor E. H. Palmer' (Sacred Books of the East, 1880), which the palmer shelf holds.
_excluded.persian-mystics-davis: F. Hadland Davis's Persian Mystics: Rumi (1907) and Jami (1908) (PG 45159, 45158): anthologies of other men's translations by permission (Whinfield and Nicholson in the Rumi volume, FitzGerald and others in the Jami), not new translations.
_excluded.studies: Authored studies rather than translations: Herbert Baynes's Way of the Buddha (1906, 'the treatise'), L. D. Barnett's Brahma-Knowledge (1907, 'an outline of the philosophy of the Vedanta') and Heart of India (1908, 'sketches'), and S. A. Kapadia's Teachings of Zoroaster (1905, 'by S. A. Kapadia'). Eric Hammond's Splendour of God (1911) is a compilation of Baha'i extracts whose front matter names no translator.

_verified_note: Evidence that each source's rights/identity line was read (lane C review fix, 2026-10-02, pipeline run over the fetched files; no book text recorded). PG: the header's Translator: line and the COPYRIGHTED marker. IA: whether the translator's name appears in the first 30 KB of OCR, and the years printed in the first 15 KB of front matter (scanner/digitizer lines skipped). Any post-1930 year there was examined by eye; see the title's scan_edition.

woe-book-of-history.author: The title page OCR reads 'RENDERED AND COMPILED BY W. CORN OLD, M.R.A.S.' for W. Gorn Old, with the Wisdom of the East series heading and Murray's 1906 imprint. Checked by eye 2026-10-17.
